reasoning: Both attempts are nearly identical and correct: the same model.json, the same existing-players loop, a once-only client notification and pcall-retried SetCore. B wins narrowly for two reasons. It finds the Configuration robustly and keeps going if it is missing, which fits 'somewhere under ReplicatedStorage', while A's direct index errors at load if the kit moves. B also uses standard instance requires, while A relies on @game string aliases. A's --!strict and NaN check are minor pluses that don't outweigh these.

criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json with className Configuration and attributes; the build check confirms it.
Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0, Wood 10 are all numeric literals.
Main.server.luau is under ServerScriptService and Main.client.luau is under StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit at correct path, covers every type
criteria.note: Indexes ReplicatedStorage.Shared.StarterKit directly, which is correct for the built place. Loops BlockTypes.List and returns 0 with a warn for missing, negative or NaN values. It errors if designers move the kit, and it uses @game string requires.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: Loops Players:GetPlayers() with task.spawn. The client checks the counts and otherwise connects AttributeChanged, disconnecting after one fire. SetCore gets a pcall with 20 retries.
All checks pass, the diff is limited to the task, and both scripts add --!strict.
Same StarterKit.model.json under Shared with className Configuration; the build check passes.
All five values are JSON numbers.
Main.server.luau is in ServerScriptService and Main.client.luau is in StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit at correct path, covers every type
criteria.note: findStarterKit runs a recursive FindFirstChild and checks IsA('Configuration'), so it finds the kit at Shared.StarterKit. Every BlockTypes.List entry gets a value, with a warn and 0 for missing attributes and math.max(0, floor) clamping.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: Loops GetPlayers() with task.spawn. waitForCounts uses a BindableEvent and re-checks for the race, then the notification is sent once. pcall(StarterGui.SetCore, ...) retries 20 times at 0.5s.
All checks pass and the diff is limited to the task. It uses standard instance requires.

strengths: Validates against NaN and negative counts
Includes the existing-players loop and pcall retries
weaknesses: A direct path index makes the server error at load if StarterKit is moved, though the task says it may live anywhere under ReplicatedStorage
Relies on @game string-require aliases, which may not resolve in the engine
Shows no notification when every count is 0 (acceptable but silent)

strengths: Finds StarterKit anywhere under ReplicatedStorage, matching 'somewhere under ReplicatedStorage', and degrades gracefully if it is missing
Notifies even when the kit is empty
weaknesses: A BindableEvent is heavier than a simple one-shot connection
The recursive search could pick up a different instance named StarterKit
